description: The shape scope of Accessible first: its answers, its usage rules and the semantic tokens it owns. The loader joins it with scheme.json.

answers.question: shape.count
answers.why: Control, badge and container corners differ.

answers.question: shape.definition
answers.why: One brand, one set of corners.

answers.question: shape.lands
answers.why: Corners show on controls and step cards.

usage.why: Clear rectangles read as fields and buttons.
Clear shapes with a word inside.
The option corner nests inside the menu, so the highlighted option reads as one clear box.
Text areas and list items keep the control corner, so people know they can type or pick there.
Slightly rounded panels read as one clear box at any zoom.
A strong edge stays visible at high zoom and for people with low vision.

usage.not: A ring that touches the control
usage.why: The gap keeps the thick ring clear of the control, so focus shows on any fill.

badge.$description: Corner of badges, chips, tooltips, keyboard keys (kbd) and checkboxes: small labels and marks.

option.$description: Corner of options in menus and lists: the panel's corner less its padding, so the corners nest.

element.$description: Corner of an element that holds content and can grow past one line: a list item, an accordion row, a text area, a calendar, an attachment, a skeleton or media.

surface.$description: Corner of cards, menus and dialogs.

open-ds.why: We use a 2px default line for borders and dividers in order to give separation and grouping that hold at any zoom. A heavier stroke does this by keeping the edge visible where a 1px line fades. So people with low vision still find each group, because strong lines separate groups (elevation.definition) and text holds AAA (accessibility.definition).

border-width.default.headline: A line you can see.
border-width.default.line: Two-pixel edges, so every field shows its shape.

radius.badge.headline: Small marks.
radius.badge.line: Badges keep a small corner, so they read as labels.

radius.control.headline: Clear control shapes.
radius.control.line: Buttons and fields have a small, plain corner.

radius.element.headline: Items that grow.
radius.element.line: Rows and text areas keep the same plain corner.

radius.option.headline: Corners that nest.
radius.option.line: An option's corner fits inside its menu's corner.

radius.surface.headline: Plain panels.
radius.surface.line: Cards and dialogs keep a small corner.
